title: The Ziggurat You See Is Mostly 1980s Reconstruction
description: Visitors often think the Ziggurat of Ur is an untouched Sumerian monument. In fact, its most visible façade and staircase were rebuilt in the 1980s under Saddam Hussein, turning the ruin into a modern showcase. The ancient core remains, but the surface you photograph is largely new.
narration: ZIGGURAT OF UR IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture an ancient, untouched step pyramid rising from the desert, a relic that survived millennia unchanged. In reality, the towering façade and its massive staircase were largely rebuilt in the 1980s on Saddam Hussein’s orders, so most of what you see is modern. Archaeologists note that the mud‑brick core is original, but the visible burnt‑brick façade and the grand staircase were rebuilt during Saddam’s 1980s heritage program. The reconstruction covered the lowest level’s façade and the monumental staircase, replacing missing bricks with new ones set in bitumen, creating the polished appearance tourists photograph today. The work was supervised by the Iraqi Department of Antiquities and cost millions of dinars, aiming to boost national pride and tourism. What you admire is a 1980s revival, not a pristine Sumerian masterpiece. It stands as a modern echo of ancient ambition.
